deep.reconstruction:
The page has two lines and continues the Euler-product computations of the previous page (fol. 69r) and the next page (fol. 70r).

Line 1: Pi(1 - (1/p)^s). The bracket is partly overwritten, but it is clearly the product over primes p of (1 - p^{-s}). This is the reciprocal of the Euler product Pi 1/(1-p^{-s}) = sum n^{-s} = zeta(s) written on fol. 69r. Expanding it by unique factorisation gives
  Pi_p (1 - p^{-s}) = 1/zeta(s) = sum_{n>=1} mu(n) n^{-s},
where mu(n) = (-1)^k if n is a product of k distinct primes, and mu(n) = 0 if n has a square factor. This expansion is my modern restatement; Riemann writes only the product and then the specialised series.

Line 2: '0 = 1 - 1/2 - 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/6 - 1/7' (sign of the 1/5 term discussed below). This is the case s = 1. Since sum 1/n diverges (zeta(s) ~ 1/(s-1), a fact noted on fol. 69r), the reciprocal product Pi(1 - 1/p) is 0. Expanding formally gives
  0 = sum mu(n)/n = 1 - 1/2 - 1/3 - 1/5 + 1/6 - 1/7 + 1/10 - 1/11 - 1/13 + 1/14 + 1/15 - ...
The term 1/4 is correctly omitted, since mu(4) = 0.

Purpose: the same Moebius sign pattern reappears on the next page as psi(1) - psi(2) - psi(3) - psi(5) + psi(6) - psi(7), and as psi(s) - psi(2s) - psi(3s) - psi(5s) + psi(6s) + psi(10s) + psi(15s) - psi(30s). There it is used to invert log zeta(s) = sum_m (1/m) sum_p p^{-ms} and so recover the prime count from a logarithmic-integral-type function. That inversion is the Moebius-inversion step of Riemann's 1859 paper. This page is a scratch check of the signs of the coefficients mu(n), or of the identity Pi(1 - 1/p) = 0 = sum mu(n)/n.
errors: As transcribed, the 1/5 term carries a plus sign. The correct sign is minus, because mu(5) = -1. In the image the sign before 1/5 looks overwritten (possibly '-' altered to '+'). On the next page Riemann writes the correct sign: psi(1) - psi(2) - psi(3) - psi(5) + psi(6) - psi(7). So either the sign was corrected or it is a momentary slip.

The step from Pi(1 - 1/p) = 0 to 0 = sum mu(n)/n is purely formal. The series is only conditionally convergent, and its value 0 lies as deep as the prime number theorem (von Mangoldt 1897). Riemann gives no justification, and none was available in 1859.

results.what: Expansion of Pi_p (1 - p^{-s}) = 1/zeta(s) as the Dirichlet series sum mu(n) n^{-s}
results.modern_name: Dirichlet series of the Moebius function / reciprocal of the Euler product
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (1737/1748); Moebius (1832) for the function and the inversion formula

results.what: sum_{n>=1} mu(n)/n = 0, obtained formally from Pi(1 - 1/p) = 0
results.modern_name: sum mu(n)/n = 0 (equivalent to the prime number theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Stated by Euler (1748); proved by von Mangoldt (1897), with a simpler proof by Landau (1899)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a formal Euler-style identity that was well known before Riemann. It is plainly preliminary to the Moebius inversion of log zeta(s) / Pi(x), which already appears in his published 1859 paper. There is no proof here, and the formal statement predates him.

checkable.asserts: The Moebius coefficients for n = 1..7 are 1, -1, -1, 0, -1, +1, -1, so the 1/5 term should carry a minus sign.
